counterexample: Let H_1 and H_2 each be the empty graph on m vertices with no edges between them, so n = 2m and M_{(1,2)} is the all-zero 2m x 2m matrix. Then Aut(M_{(1,2)}) = S_{2m}, of order (2m)! , which is superpolynomial in n. But by construction alpha_1 is a subset of gamma_1, whose size is at most |beta_1|*|beta_2| <= n^3 * n^3 = n^6 (line 0024/0032). Hence alpha_1 cannot equal Aut(M_{(1,2)}). Moreover every element of gamma_1 is a direct product pi_1 x pi_2 preserving the vertex blocks, so no automorphism of M_{(1,2)} that moves a vertex of H_1 into H_2 (e.g. the transposition of one vertex of H_1 with one of H_2) can ever lie in alpha_1, whatever the oracle sets beta_1, beta_2 are.
